审校 e1、e2：确认 Jorganos Archer 为男性具名弓手，采用“约加诺斯弓手”；将 Bow of Jorganos 统一为“约加诺斯之弓”，并补足两条术语理由的原文依据。未发现需隔离或新增项。
已核对 e1：确认 King Heort 指奥兰斯传说君王兼立法者，译名采用“赫奥特王”，并补全 term_reason 以说明其身份与使用范围；无需隔离或新增。
已审校分配条目 e1：Chalana Arroy 为格洛兰萨神话中的治疗与慈悲女神、Arroin 之母；保留专名“查拉娜阿罗伊”，不加间隔号，归入 characters 的女神专名。四维核对通过，并补齐 term_reason 以说明神祇身份与职能。未发现 audit findings。
本批仅审 e1：确认 Eurmal 为神祇专名，标准译名定为欧尔马尔，保留 characters/proper_name 与 required 级别，并修正术语说明以反映其诡术/混乱神格及祝福、诅咒机制。
已逐条核对 e1-e6 的来源、译名、分类与一致性。e2 补齐 Kallyr 缺失的 enforcement、term_kind 与 term_reason；e6 依据 20590 的男性指称修正性别并更新 term_reason。f1 所涉全称变体与原名同指 Chinkis Mor，同译“钦基斯莫尔”成立，不是不同专名冲突。
审校 3 个角色专名：保留“羽马女王”，修正温科特父名译法与乌罗克斯称号语序；分类、性别与证据一致。
已审 e1-e12：确认温科特、赫奥特、萨拉斯卡、因金等专名；修正御云者、德里克剥皮者/独径及温科特王，并将普通头衔 Emperor 隔离。
已审校 e1-e12，逐一核对来源、译名、分类与跨批共享译名。f1-f5 均为同一人物或神祇的全名/短名、称号与核心名共用译名，未发现不同实体误合。修正 e1 的 Nallindia 音译为女性名用字娜林迪娅，保留 Trailblazer 译作开路者；其余条目保留原推荐译名。
完成 e1 的术语审校：Humakt 为格洛兰萨神祇专名，原文明确称其为 the god of Death / Lord of Death，并兼有战争、誓言与荣誉职能；确认标准译名为“胡马科特”，分类“其他”合法，proper_name 下 required 正确，候选音译变体统一到该译名，无新增、隔离或修订项。
已核 e1-e3 的原文、译名、分类与一致性；Dark Woman、Vevkoban the Chaos Horse、Ves Venna 均保留为 required 专名。补正 e1、e3 的 term_reason；f1 中 e3/e4 为同一人物 Ves Venna 的短名与完整头衔，不构成异名共用译名错误。
审校 e1：确认 Elmal 为神祇专名，保留标准译名“埃尔马尔”；将 terms 分类由“身份”修正为“其他”，并补充可核实的 term_reason。本批无隔离、新增或 allow_no_match 项。

evidence.text: “Elmal Guards the Stead”

Decide which is your clan's most important deity: Orlanth, Ernalda, or Elmal. The game is slightly easier if Orlanth is your main god, but if you would rather be devoted to the Earth Mother or the Sun Defender, here's your chance. The game starts with a temple for the deity chosen here.

The gods we worship are: Barntar the Plowman; Chalana Arroy the Healer; Elmal god of the Sun; Ernalda, Orlanth's wife and Queen of the Earth; Eurmal the Trickster; Humakt, god of War and Death; Issaries, god of Trade, Travel, and Conciliation; Lhankor Mhy, god of Lawspeaking and Knowledge; Maran Gor, goddess of Earthquakes and Destruction; Odayla, god of Hunting; Orlanth, King of the Gods, and god of Storm; Uralda the Cow Mother; Urox, also called Storm Bull, berserker Chaos-fighter; Vinga the Adventuress. Some are not important enough to build a shrine to: Gustbran the Smith; Heler, god of Rain; Minlinster the Brewer; Mralota the Pig Mother; Nevala the Sheep Mother; Yinkin, god of Alynxes.

When they went over hills, they followed his hawk.

In one place, the goddess Ernalda gave her priestess Hareva a unique type of winter-grown grapes. The wine made from these grapes was a very pale yellow, and always cool to taste. So Colymar and Hareva called that place Clearwine, and made it their home. There they hunted and built houses to face the coming winter. Normally, good Orlanthi try to avoid looking at the Chaotic red moon that hangs in the northern sky. But one night your holy people notice that great, black scars have appeared on its surface. This means something of great import, surely.
The moon… something will happen to the Red Moon soon.

We are living in a good time, then. We reckon that it is now the Third Age. We know that if we are not vigilant, bad people will rise up yet again. Is the Pharaoh, who drove us from our homes in Heortland, part of a new wave of dangerous enemies, or is he merely another unjust ruler? Is the strange Red Moon that rose in the sky about a hundred years ago a harbinger of bad times? We don't know yet. So we wait and watch, and meanwhile tend our herds, plant our fields, and raid our neighbors, as any good Orlanthi should.

One reason the world is no longer as good is that Chaos is still around us. Some say it is even getting worse. The foul goat-men known as broos are still everywhere; some say they lurk in Dragon Pass. Wherever there is disease, there is Malia. In the darkest places of the world skulk ogres, scorpion men, vampires, walktapi, and harpies. Some misguided individuals secretly worship Chaos gods; they may steal people’s heads in the name of Thanatar, or hatch intrigues and conspiracies in the name of Krarsht. A new, red moon rose in the sky a hundred years ago; it stinks so much of Chaos that it gave our holy people headaches, at first.

evidence.text: The dwarf’s dead god Mostal was foe to Orlanth.
The dwarfs worship a dead god named Mostal. They try to confuse people by saying that Mostal is not a god at all, but an idea called The World Machine.

The bad people of the Second Age were the God Learners. They were sorcerers from the far west, where they don't believe that gods and spirits are real, and regularly rob them of their life force with cruel magic. The God Learners tried to enslave all peoples, and to promote the worship of their own fake deities over everyone's real gods. They made a parody of the god Mostal, who is the Maker. To hurt Mostal more, it was constructed without respect or dignity, and so although it could do almost anything that a real god could do, it was not living. It was Zistor, a huge monster, made of gleaming metal and wires. It had an island called Machine City. Everyone in Machine City worked to make themselves into better parts of the machine, or to make the machine better. And that way Zistor grew. And somewhere, sometime, the machine belief of Zistor became a god. And when that occurred, then Orlanth could act, by himself. For as everyone knows, every god and goddess of Glorantha is bound by their promises at the Compromise. None of them may ever step out of their natural being, unless the destruction of the universe is imminent. Orlanth helped our ancestors destroy Zistor and the Machine City. Many of our ancestors died in this war, but there could be no better death than to die stopping bad people from destroying the world. This happened about four hundred years ago.

Time is the Cosmic Compromise. It was birthed at the Dawn, by Arachne Solara, at the climax of Orlanth's Lightbringers Quest. Before that, things did not always happen in a single order. Sometimes things happened different ways at the same time. Sometimes a thing would break, then fall, then it would be whole again. It's hard for us to imagine how things were back then, for we are children of time and can no more imagine a world without it than we could breathe in a world without air. The gods understood things back then, but now even they are bound by time. They cannot intervene in our world now, with limited exceptions. Instead of doing things themselves, they watch us do things for them. We call on them for aid through prayer, ritual, and heroquesting. If this Compromise is ever broken, Chaos will come back into the world. Now things always happen in one order, in one particular way. This is what we call history.

The agreement of Orlanth and Yelm is called The Cosmic Compromise. It brings into being a new goddess, Arachne Solara, who weaves a net and shows the gods how to use it. With her net, they bind the Devil, and she drains it of its force, until it is just a husk.

evidence.text: Time is the Cosmic Compromise. It was birthed at the Dawn, by Arachne Solara, at the climax of Orlanth's Lightbringers Quest. Before that, things did not always happen in a single order. Sometimes things happened different ways at the same time. Sometimes a thing would break, then fall, then it would be whole again. It's hard for us to imagine how things were back then, for we are children of time and can no more imagine a world without it than we could breathe in a world without air. The gods understood things back then, but now even they are bound by time. They cannot intervene in our world now, with limited exceptions. Instead of doing things themselves, they watch us do things for them. We call on them for aid through prayer, ritual, and heroquesting. If this Compromise is ever broken, Chaos will come back into the world. Now things always happen in one order, in one particular way. This is what we call history.

This agreement between the gods is called the Cosmic Compromise. All of the deities agreed to share the world with each other, and with all of the experiences which they had already had. No one was allowed to avoid what they did not like, and so all of the gods agreed that they would share their time among both Life and Death. They agreed that they would not actively intervene in each other's realms except in those ways which they had already done. They would not individually or consciously alter the world. They would not even turn their awareness to it, unless called upon to do so.
